svg.title: GitHub access: issuance, delivery and renewal
svg.desc: The repository sequence diagram with private account labels anonymized. The host verifies VM identity, uses owner-bound GitHub Apps, journals scoped tokens, delivers them, then revokes predecessors. Optional organization discovery and failure handling are retained.

g.text: GitHub: verified VM, owner-bound Apps, repository-scoped tokens
Initial delivery and each active-instance renewal (about every 30 minutes)
Failed QGA or identity check: stop before any GitHub mint.
Preserve the private ledger and previous guest token store.
User A and Org B each have their own
private App, signing key and owner-bound installation.
App JWTs expire nine minutes from signing.
Repeat discovery on each renewal so future organization
repositories join the approved policy. No discovery token
Failed predecessor revocations remain in the ledger for retry.
Failed delivery: keep grants journaled; do not revoke predecessors.
A response can be lost after the atomic write; inspect before retry.
Write profile: contents, pull requests and issues write.
App keys stay on Proxmox; no personal GitHub login/PAT is copied.
The public harness clone needs no GitHub credential.
